title: Metro Manila Family Day Out Starter Pack
hook: Three spots that make the toddler, the teen, and the grandparents happy in one go.
body: Planning a family day out in Metro Manila usually means a group chat that goes nowhere. Skip the chaos and stick to these classics that satisfy every age group. From colonial history to sharks swimming over your head, your Friday is sorted. Bring your walking shoes and prepare to capture every moment. If you can keep the group together until the last stop, consider it a win. Let’s get out the door before everyone changes their mind!

title: Things to do in Metro Manila: The 24-Hour Plan
hook: Start with 1594 dumplings in Binondo and end with Michelin-starred dining in Makati. Zero wasted hours today!
body: Start early on Ongpin Street with hot dumplings and sweet hopia in one of the world's oldest Chinatowns. By early afternoon, explore Fort Santiago to walk the Baluarte de Santa Barbara overlooking the Pasig River and see the historic dungeons. Wrap up your Thursday night at The Alley at Karrivin in Makati, where Toyo Eatery serves a one-Michelin-star dinner made entirely with Philippine ingredients. Grab your shoes and go right now!

sticker: Hidden Gem vs The Famous One
title: Rainy day activities in Metro Manila: 2 picks
hook: Makati gives you sixty tiny diorama worlds. Las Piñas counters with an entire bamboo organ backroom!
body: When afternoon showers threaten your plans, pick your indoor vibe. The glossy crowd-pleaser is Ayala Museum at Greenbelt, packing sixty detailed diorama worlds into a sleek space renovated by Leandro V. Locsin Partners. Down south, the humble hero is Bamboo Organ Museum beside St. Joseph Parish, displaying historical objects that reveal how the famous instrument was actually built and restored. Do you want polished Makati dioramas or quiet Las Piñas history? Head out today!

body: Option one: hop on a bangka from Mactan and let fish swarm around you in the shallow water off Nalusuan, then grab seafood barbecue on Pandanon sandbar. Option two: climb into the Busay hills to the Roman-style Temple of Leah and strike poses among concrete columns built for love. Are we doing salty snorkels or mountain emperor vibes? Cast your vote and get moving today!

title: Fun things to do in Calabarzon this weekend
hook: Two boatmen push your canoe upstream over rapids while you hold on for dear life!
body: Saturday is here, and your group chat needs an actual plan. Head to Calabarzon today for serious water thrills. In Pagsanjan, two boatmen push your narrow canoe against river rapids into a deep gorge. Over in Mauban, catch a boat to Cagbalete Island where low tide exposes a huge sandbar into Lamon Bay. Or gear up with a headlamp in Cavinti to wade through a chest-deep river inside a cave. Pack your dry bag and go!
